title: Navigator Arc: workspace federation and contextual switchbar for compact consoles
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Problem: The current left-rail + modal switch flows in Redwood Console create deep context switching for customers who manage multiple teams, models and rollout policies. Edge cases include: 1) frequent workspace switching during canary rollouts, 2) comparing cost breakdowns across workspaces, and 3) loss of quick access to rollout controls while inspecting model dashboards.

Goal: Design a compact, persistent contextual switchbar (Navigator Arc) and a lightweight federation of workspace lenses that keeps the most relevant controls and cost lenses visible without adding vertical chrome. The design should: (a) reduce average time-to-target when switching workspace/context for common tasks (deployments, rollouts, cost analysis), (b) keep consoles under 1200px width usable, and (c) be accessible and keyboard-navigable.

Scope: IA and navigation pattern (no final visual polish). Includes low-fidelity flows, two interactive prototypes (desktop narrow and wide), a usability script, and handoff spec for frontend engineering and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Navigator Arc persists across Console pages and does not overlap native top nav.
Workspace lenses (Metadata, Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost) can be pinned per-workspace and exposed in the Arc with one click.
Switch operations complete within 300ms in prototype (network emulation) and maintain focus context for keyboard users.
Design tokens provided: spacing, z-index, motion duration; component spec for Arc + lens chips in Figma.
Prototype tested with 6 internal reviewers and 8 external participants; results documented and critical issues triaged.
Handoff includes per-route accessibility notes and suggested telemetry events for product/analytics team.
tasks: Design: low-fi flows for Arc + three lens states (collapsed, expanded, pinned)
Prototype: build two interactive Figma prototypes (narrow 1024px, wide 1440px)
Research: run remote usability test (script + 8 external participants)
Engineering sync: review runtime constraints with ENG infra (batching of switch requests)
Docs: create Confluence spec + PRD reference section for Console-IA-Refactor
Handoff: token list, component states, aria roles and keyboard mapping
discussion: 2026-02-12 - Marisol: Kickoff with PM and infra. Shared initial pain evidence from support tickets (links below). Proposal to keep Arc non-modal so it never traps keyboard focus.

2026-02-19 - Design critique: Reduced left-rail width and introduced the Arc as a horizontal affordance. Engineering flagged single-click route prep as a potential perf hotspot; Ibrahim to prototype lightweight route prefetching.
2026-02-25 - PM check-in (Ava): Prioritize rollouts tab and cost lens pinning because enterprise customers requested side-by-side cost comparisons during canary rollouts.

2026-03-02 - Usability pilot completed: 8 participants. Key finding: participants expected workspace switch to preserve the last open lens (e.g., if they were in Rollouts, switching should land them in Rollouts for the new workspace). We added a persistent per-user preference for lens restore.
2026-03-08 - Accessibility review: keyboard skip link proposed; ensure Arc chip order is deterministic and announceable to screen readers.

2026-03-10 - Engineering follow-up: ENG will add an endpoint to pre-warm route metadata; suggested to batch up to 5 prefetch requests and fall back to cached metadata if network slow. Ibrahim to open ENG-22144 for the infra change.
review_feedback: PM (Ava S.) - Strongly prefer having explicit 'Pin for workspace' affordance. Concern: too many pinned lenses could crowd Arc. Suggest max 4 pinned chips + overflow menu.

Eng (Ibrahim P.) - Likes the non-blocking Arc. Requests that Arc state be driven by URL so we can deep-link into a pinned lens + rollout step. Also requested telemetry events on 'switch.start' and 'switch.complete'.
Security (Lena R.) - No additional security gating required for the Arc itself, but calls that trigger private model metadata must respect VPC scoping. Add note for Private deployment handbook.
Design (Rory T.) - Visual weight: reduce motion for collapse/expand to 120ms. Use token 'motion-quick' to align with console patterns.
decisions: Keep Arc outside of the left-rail; it will anchor to the top content area directly below the global header to avoid overlapping global navigation.
Default state: Arc shows workspace name + up to three pinned lens chips + a chevron to expand to full lens menu.
Behavior: workspace switch will restore the last-open lens if the user preference 'restore_lens_on_switch' is true; otherwise default to Metadata lens.
Performance: engineering will implement a prefetch endpoint; Arc will show a skeleton placeholder if prefetch latency > 200ms.
Accessibility: Arc chips will be buttons with aria-pressed states and a roving tabindex implementation for keyboard navigation.
next_steps: Finalize responsive specs and hand off Figma component variants (by 2026-03-16)
ENG-22144: Infra prefetch endpoint (Ibrahim to open and link) — dependency for release planning
Product: add telemetry doc for switch events and cost-lens usage (Ava assigned)
Run a second round of usability tests focusing on overflow behavior and keyboard-only flows (target 10 participants)
Prepare a phased rollout plan: alpha internal opt-in → beta to select customers → full release (tie to console-2026.05 release window)
